I personally buy into companies that I believe in. Companies that are doing things I think will lead to success and/or led by people who I think know what they are doing. However, I only invest as a hobby and treat investing what it truly is, gambling.

Buy mutual funds with a focus on broad market exposure and low fees, e.g. Vanguard's Target Date Funds.

Do not buy individual stocks. That's straight up gambling at that point.

You finally have money, and there's a good chance you won't have money if you try to pick stocks. You're much better off investing in an index mutual fund. That way if one stock fails, other stocks in the index can make up for it. This is called diversity. Only once you're adequately diversified would I look into picking individual stocks, and even then I'd never play the stock market this way with money I couldn't afford to lose.
